capex_to_revenue.why: Pooled history is 19.6%. 2026 guidance of $2.25 to $2.35 billion on about 10.7 billion of revenue gives about 21%, and capex must keep production flat or growing.

quotes.quote: If we fail to find, develop or acquire additional oil, NGLs and natural gas reserves, our reserves and production will decline materially from their current levels.

fade_years.why: Reserves and production decline without continued drilling and acquisitions, and the company is adding Montney and Permian inventory, so margins and growth converge to steady state over about 10 years.

long_run_op_margin.why: The company's own history is 17.3% in 2024 and 12.7% in 2025, with 2026 prices well above 2025 levels. Cyclical base rates say a margin above the median keeps only about half of the gap, so I use about 19%, slightly above the roughly 17% median.

op_margin.why: Nine-month 2026 operating income of 1,117 is held down by 1,485 of impairments, while Q3 with no impairments was 877 on 2,602 of revenue, about 34%. I assume year 1 is about 17.5% including those impairments, then a high but fading margin as prices normalize and some ceiling-test charges recur.

quotes.quote: Base year: return on tangible capital 0.0715
for an average cost of $1.3 million to $1.7 million per 10,000 foot equivalent drilling location

return_on_new_investment_long_run.why: The base-year return on tangible capital of 7.15% is below the 7.64% break-even and reflects impairments. Cheap inventory adds, at $1.3 to $1.7 million per location, and cube-development efficiency support a modest premium over break-even, so I use 9%.

rev_growth.why: Year 1 (2026) is far above the base year. Nine-month revenue is 8,147 against 8,908 for all of 2025, helped by NuVista and higher prices, so I put 2026 at about 10.7 billion, roughly +20%. After that growth slows because prices should normalize, Anadarko is gone, and Logan plus acreage adds are partly offset by depletion.

terminal_growth.why: A mature North American E&P with a depleting reserve base that must keep reinvesting should grow below the 3.75% anchor, so I use 2.5%.

risks.risk: Oil and gas prices fall back from 2026 levels and ceiling-test impairments recur
Growth stalls after the portfolio changes: the Logan deal fails or underperforms, the Montney midstream outage persists, and volumes decline
Returns on new investment fall toward or below break-even as inventory costs and transport and processing costs rise

debt_level_representative.why: Debt of 5,202 at year-end 2025 fell to 3,588 after Anadarko sale proceeds were used to retire debt, so the base-year level overstates the debt the company now carries.

situation.margin_position: The 2025 GAAP operating margin of 12.7% is depressed by non-cash full-cost ceiling-test impairments ($920 million). Before impairments the margin is much higher. Realized prices in 2026 are well above 2025 (Q3 WTI 85.79 against 64.93), so the current underlying margin is above the company's own median.

tax_rate_representative.why: The 2025 rate of 0.1683 came with a tax recovery, while the nine months of 2026 show tax of 141 on pretax earnings of 516, so the sustainable rate is higher.

situation.why: Base-year operating income carries $920 million of impairments, and margins have swung from -88.7% in 2020 to 28.5% in 2018. In 2026 nine-month revenue is already 8,147 against 8,908 for all of 2025, and the portfolio changed with NuVista in and Anadarko out. Elevated oil prices in 2026 should partly mean-revert. Impairments recur under full-cost accounting, so I fade the margin toward about the long-run median rather than the 2026 Q3 level.

quotes.quote: Pooled over those years: capital expenditure / revenue 0.1964

capex_to_revenue.why: 2026 capital guidance of $2,250 to $2,350 million is about 21% of expected 2026 revenue of roughly $10.7 billion. This is above the 19.6% pooled ratio because maintaining volumes in shale needs steady drilling, and it will rise if prices fall.

quotes.quote: Under the terms and conditions of the Arrangement Agreement, Ovintiv Canada will acquire all of the issued and outstanding common shares of Logan

fade_years.why: Moving from peak-price margins to mid-cycle takes several years, and the Logan and NuVista inventory extends the runway, so I use a 10-year fade.

long_run_op_margin.why: This is a commodity-price cyclical. Ex-impairment margins were about 22-23% in 2024-25, and the history shows 26% in 2023 and 17% in 2024. I fade to about 19%, above the 5-year GAAP median of 17%, because full-cost impairments recur in down cycles and gas weighting raises unit midstream cost.

op_margin.why: Year 1 blends a first half with $1,485 million of nine-month impairments and a Q3 margin of about 34%. After that, margin stays high in year 2 and fades as prices normalize and transport and processing costs per BOE rise with the Canadian gas mix.

quotes.quote: Return on new investment at which growth adds no value (code, after the company's leverage): 0.0764.
for an average cost of $1.3 million to $1.7 million per 10,000 foot equivalent drilling location

return_on_new_investment_long_run.why: The base-year return on tangible capital is 7.2%, below the 7.6% break-even. Recent inventory is bought cheaply, at $1.3 to $1.7 million per location, and the cube development model supports efficiency. Acquisition-priced and depleting shale returns are still only modestly above the cost of capital, so I use 9%.

quotes.quote: Average oil and plant condensate prices increased 27 percent and 31 percent, respectively, primarily due to higher benchmark prices.

rev_growth.why: Year 1 (FY2026) jumps about 20%. Nine-month revenue is 8,147 and Q3 alone is 2,602, with NuVista added and Anadarko sold in April. Year 2 dips because Anadarko is absent for the full year and I assume oil prices ease from the Q3 peak, partly offset by Logan volumes. Growth then runs low-single-digit, since inventory is being added at low cost.

quotes.quote: Cost of equity r 0.0841; long-run nominal growth anchor g_anchor 0.0375.

terminal_growth.why: Mature North American E&P with a depleting asset base needs continuous reinvestment. I set growth below the 3.75% anchor at 3%, with inventory additions supporting it.

risks.risk: Oil prices fall back from the Middle East-driven peak, or the extended-decline scenario in the 10-K occurs, causing margin compression and further ceiling-test impairments.
Prices and volumes disappoint (Montney midstream outage persists, Logan fails to close or underperforms), so revenue stalls.
Reinvestment returns on acquired and drilled inventory fall to roughly the cost of capital as acquisition prices rise and Canadian gas weighting increases.

debt_level_representative.why: Debt was 5,202 at year-end 2025 and fell to 3,588 after Anadarko proceeds were used to repay debt, though the pending all-cash Logan deal of about $890 million will add some back.

situation.margin_position: The 2025 GAAP operating margin of 12.7% is depressed by $920 million of non-cash ceiling-test impairments. Before impairments it was about 23%. In 2026 the margin is rising because realized oil and condensate prices are well above 2025 (WTI $85.79 in Q3 versus $64.93). The Q3 margin was about 34% with no impairment. That is a commodity-price peak, not a structural level.

tax_rate_representative.why: The 2025 tax result was a recovery (-472 on pretax 770), while 2026 nine-month tax is 141 on 516 pretax, about 27%, and Q3 is about 32%, so 16.8% will not persist.

situation.why: FY2025 had low benchmark prices and large impairments, so reported margin understates normal profitability. FY2026 (year 1) already looks very different: nine-month revenue is 8,147 against 6,761, and Q3 operating income is 877. The portfolio has also changed. Anadarko was sold, NuVista added, Logan is pending, and the business is now more gas-weighted and Canadian, with higher transport and processing cost per BOE. I assume prices and margins fall back toward a mid-cycle level that still sits above the 5-year median.

business_model.claim: Ovintiv is an oil and natural gas exploration and production company with assets in the United States and Canada. It also markets oil, NGLs and natural gas.
quotes: Ovintiv is a leading North American oil and natural gas exploration and production company that is focused on developing its multi-basin portfolio of high-quality assets located in the United States and Canada.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item for 2025. The change since is inferred from the 2026 portfolio changes.
business_model.claim: There are two reportable segments, USA Operations and Canadian Operations. In 2025 the USA segment accounted for 64 percent of upstream production revenues, excluding hedging, and Canada for 36 percent.
quotes: USA Operations includes the exploration for, development of, and production and marketing of oil, NGLs, natural gas and other related activities within the United States, which includes Permian in west Texas and Anadarko in west-central Oklahoma.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items (revenue lines from F2, the revenue-source sentence from P3)
business_model.claim: Revenue comes mainly from selling produced oil, NGLs and natural gas. In the nine months to Sep. 30, 2026, total revenues were 8,147 (table in millions). That total was made up of product and service revenues of 6,733, sales of purchased product of 1,274, net risk-management gains of 86 and sublease revenues of 54.
quotes: Ovintiv’s revenues are substantially derived from sales of oil, NGLs and natural gas production.

business_model.claim: Commodity prices are the main revenue driver. In the first nine months of 2026, higher realized oil and plant condensate prices lifted upstream product revenues, with oil up 27 percent and plant condensate up 31 percent.
quotes: Average oil and plant condensate prices increased 27 percent and 31 percent, respectively, primarily due to higher benchmark prices.
Our financial performance and condition are substantially dependent on the prevailing prices we receive for the oil, NGLs and natural gas which we produce.

business_model.claim: Production volume is the second revenue driver, and it moves with acquisitions, divestitures and drilling. The 2026 NuVista acquisition raised plant condensate and natural gas volumes. The Anadarko sale lowered oil volumes.
quotes: Plant condensate and natural gas production volumes increased primarily due to the NuVista Acquisition in the first quarter of 2026.

business_model.claim: Third-quarter 2026 production averaged about 631 MBOE/d, made up of 204 Mbbls/d of oil and condensate, 83 Mbbls/d of other NGLs and 2,062 MMcf/d of natural gas. Production is therefore split between liquids and natural gas.
quotes: Third quarter average total production volumes were approximately 631 MBOE/d, including 204 Mbbls/d of oil and condensate, 83 Mbbls/d of other NGLs (C2 to C4) and 2,062 MMcf/d of natural gas

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items for the purpose. The small spread is inferred from F2.
business_model.claim: A marketing line buys and resells third-party product. This line produced 343 of sales against 333 of purchased-product expense in Q3 2026 (table in millions). The company says it provides flexibility around transportation commitments and delivery points.
quotes: Revenues from the sale of purchased product relate to activities that provide operational flexibility and cost mitigation for transportation commitments, product type, delivery points and customer diversification within the USA and Canadian Operations segments.

business_model.claim: Hedging adds a revenue line and is used to dampen price swings. Net risk-management gains were 27 in Q3 2026 and 86 in the nine months (table in millions).
quotes: The Company enters into derivative financial instruments to mitigate price volatility and provide more certainty around cash flows.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (F2 income statement)
business_model.claim: The main cash operating costs are transportation and processing, lease operating expense, production taxes and purchased product. Upstream transportation and processing cost $8.34 per BOE in the nine months of 2026, up $203 million on 2025, mainly because of NuVista volumes. This shows that adding Canadian gas-weighted volumes raises midstream cost.

business_model.basis: stated in P2 for the risk. The full-cost basis is stated in F1. Impairment amounts are from F2.
